physicalEvidence.summary: The complete soft-snake paper executes a pretrained PPOC goal controller with contact-aware Matsuoka CPG feedback on a real pneumatic snake with magnetic tactile sensors. The primary manuscript was revised November 2023, and the PI reports January 2025 T-RO acceptance; this is not a new 2025/2026 experiment. Coauthors and hardware are linked to WPI; Fu independently identifies lead author Xuan Liu as her former PhD student. Physical20, without implying current UF access.

physicalEvidence.summary: The May 2025 full harvesting paper uses finetuned YOLOv8n-seg, depth-derived fruit poses and classical arm planning on a DJI Matrice350 bimanual platform. Real orchard fruit trials hold the UAV static while detection guides the arms. The integrated airborne demonstration manually positions/hovers the UAV and harvests an artificial fruit; it does not establish autonomous orchard flight. Peduncle position is a fixed offset and the detected pose is not continuously updated. The work is explicitly UCR. Current UHCL hardware inventory does not independently prove a new learned deployment. Physical20.

name: Daniel Bruder
title: Assistant Professor
fitReason: Leading methodological work combining learned residual dynamics with physical models for soft-robot manipulation.

physicalEvidence.status: Prior-host or collaborative learned robot verified; current-site learned execution unverified
physicalEvidence.summary: The complete NASA-hosted accepted manuscript combines a physics-based Koopman model with a learned residual model in MPC. It runs on a three-joint pneumatic soft arm with six muscle inputs and motion-capture feedback for trajectory tracking, pick-and-place and dry-erase writing. The paper appeared online October 2024 and in a 2025 issue; it is not a fresh 2026 experiment. Bruder is first/corresponding author with Michigan affiliation, with Harvard coauthors and prior collaborative hardware provenance. Current Michigan ownership/access was not independently established, so physical20.
